content: ## Purpose
This page sets the 2027 monthly close for usage-based invoices: when each month's invoices are cut, which usage lands in which invoice period, and how late usage is handled. Billing Ops, Telemetry and Support use it when a customer asks what a month's invoice covers.
## Monthly close calendar
| Business day | Step | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| BD1 | Usage for the closed month is frozen in the metering warehouse | Telemetry |
| BD2 | Usage is rated against the account's price book and invoice lines are drafted | Billing Ops |
| BD3 | Variance review: lines more than 25% above the prior month are checked against usage | Billing Ops |
| BD4 | Invoices are issued and autopay is attempted on the due date shown on the invoice | Billing Ops |
| BD5 | Revenue for the month is booked and the period is closed | Accounting |"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/token-estimates-for-sales-quotes-2026.json", "chunk": "1/1", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Estimating Token Volumes for Sales Quotes", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-09", "text": "title: Estimating Token Volumes for Sales Quotes

body: ## Purpose
How solutions engineers estimate a prospect's monthly tokens before a quote. Estimates use an approximate tokenizer and round up 10% for safety. This page is about forecasting before purchase. It does not explain how billed tokens are counted on an invoice; for that, see the token accounting pages and the billing routing page.
## Method
1. Sample 100 representative requests.
2. Count characters and divide by 4 for English text.
3. Multiply by expected monthly volume and add 10%.
_Last reviewed 2026-02-09._"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/hosted-api-packages-free-tier-and-overage-policy.json", "chunk": "3/16", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Hosted API Packages: Free Tier, Included Usage, and Overage Policy", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-26", "text": "(continued) ### Metered quantities
- For embeddings, usage is metered in billed tokens for the embedding input. (We also store vector count/dimensions for ops, but packaging is based on billed tokens unless otherwise stated in an order form.)
### What “included usage” means
Included usage is the amount bundled with a package **during a billing period**. Charges apply only when:
1) a customer is on a plan that allows overage, and
2) usage exceeds included amounts.
### Billing period
- Self-serve: monthly, aligned to subscription start date (unless otherwise stated).
- Contracted enterprise: per order form.
---"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/discounting-and-credits-policy-for-usage-based-products.json", "chunk": "9/20", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Discounting and Credits Policy for Usage-Based Products", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-22", "text": "### Application order (standard)
On each invoice, the billing system applies adjustments in this order:
1. **Included usage** in the customer’s package/free tier (if applicable)
2. **Contracted unit prices** (including any negotiated discount)
3. **Credits** (promotional/contracted/service), applied to the eligible usage subtotal
4. Taxes and non-creditable line items
Important: credits offset charges; they do **not change recorded usage quantities**.
### Cache-hit attribution and billed tokens
If the meter spec distinguishes cached vs uncached billed tokens, credits apply to the final **billed** quantities after cache and dedupe logic. Any customer-visible statement about caching must use approved language from Legal (see related page)."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/hosted-api-packages-free-tier-and-overage-policy.json", "chunk": "11/16", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Hosted API Packages: Free Tier, Included Usage, and Overage Policy", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-26", "text": "## Customer-facing wording guidelines (approved language)
### Principles
- Use **billed tokens** as the primary unit.
- Emphasize predictability and transparency.
- Avoid internal implementation details (retries, fallbacks, raw token counts) unless required for a specific incident.
### Approved phrases (use these)
- “We bill based on **billed tokens**, which reflect the tokens processed to generate and deliver your responses.”
- “Streaming responses are billed as a single request, and billed tokens reflect the output delivered.”
- “Your plan includes X billed tokens per month. If you exceed that amount, you’ll either be charged overage (paid plans) or asked to upgrade (Free).”
- “You can view billed token usage by day/model/region in the Console and export via the Usage API.”"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/discounting-and-credits-policy-for-usage-based-products.json", "chunk": "3/20", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Discounting and Credits Policy for Usage-Based Products", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-22", "text": "## Definitions (use these terms consistently)
- **Meter / billable unit:** The unit recorded by billing telemetry and used to produce invoices. Example: **billed_tokens** for Hosted API.
- **Raw tokens vs billed tokens:** Raw tokens may include uncached or pre-dedupe counts. **Billed tokens** are the invoicing unit after billing rules (dedupe/idempotency, cache-hit attribution rules, etc.). Credits and discounts apply to **billed** usage only.
- **Discount:** A reduction in price per unit (e.g., $/1M tokens) or a percentage reduction on usage charges.
- **Credit:** A dollar value that offsets charges on invoices (a “coupon” balance). Credits have **no cash value** and are not refundable unless required by contract or law.
- **Service credit:** A credit issued for SLA/non-conformance or billing errors.
- **Promotional credit:** A credit granted for trial, marketing campaigns, partnerships, or sales incentives.
- **Contracted credit:** A credit explicitly included in an Order Form/MSA as part of commercial terms."}]}

body: ## Symptom
The Console invoice list sorts by the date an invoice was issued, not the period it covers, so a re-issued invoice for an earlier month can appear at the top.
## Workaround
Use the period filter or read the period on each invoice. Amounts and lines are correct.
## Status
Fix planned for the Console release in May 2027.
